exposure: Cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing
cesarean delivery (CD) for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing (NRFHT)
outcome: Composite adverse neonatal outcomes (Apgar <5 at 5 min, seizures, mechanical ventilation, sepsis, intraventricular hemorrhage, necrotizing enterocolitis, or neonatal death)
Composite adverse maternal outcomes (endometritis, blood transfusion, wound complication, admission to intensive care unit, thromboembolism, hysterectomy, or death)
cohort: 7310 singleton pregnancies between 37.0 and 41.6 weeks gestation who underwent cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing
finding: Several risk factors were identified for both composite adverse neonatal outcomes and composite adverse maternal outcomes following cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing, but the models had limited ability to predict these outcomes.
mod_finding: Among singletons between 37 and 41 weeks who labored, the rate of cesarean delivery (CD) for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing (NRFHT) was about 3.7%.
